She sought to fill the void, but her loom lacked color. One day, she wept, and her tears—glistening with the memory of the first dawn—fell into the abyss. As they drifted through the nothingness, they shattered into a billion iridescent shards.

A mischievous spirit, Wind-Walker, caught the fragments. He didn’t want them to vanish, so he blew them deep into the velvet fabric of the night. Each shard lodged itself firmly, glowing with a persistent, stubborn heat. "These are the eyes of the ancestors," he whispered, "watching over the world when the sun retreats."

The Weaver looked up, satisfied. She had intended to create a tapestry, but she had instead created a map. Even now, when travelers lose their way in the dark, they look toward those scattered tears. They follow the light of the Weaver’s grief, finding their home in the constellations she accidentally birthed, proving that beauty often emerges from the most profound depths of sorrow. She smiled at the heavens, knowing the void was filled with her own heart.
